exemplar_texts.0: The right to refuse: the clones' rebellion is about consent, so the story asks whether a copy can say no.
exemplar_texts.1: Primes improve by retelling: the hologram repeats and embellishes stories, so memory becomes editable and grief becomes co-authorship.
exemplar_texts.2: The trust that cannot be exited: members cannot withdraw without losing their stake, so commitment is total.
exemplar_texts.3: The ongoing relationship with the dead: a mourner keeps talking to the deceased, so grief is maintenance rather than closure.
exemplar_texts.4: The comfortable family home: the setting is calm and affluent, so the drama is entirely in what is not said.
exemplar_texts.5: The veto window: a person can cancel a prepared action in the instant before execution, so freedom is relocated from initiation to refusal.
exemplar_texts.6: The distributed body: nutrients flow through the network to wherever they are needed, so the organism has no center to decapitate.
exemplar_texts.7: The widow and the copy: the protagonist cannot accept the android because it lacks the dead man's flaws, so love is defined by imperfection.
exemplar_texts.8: The human cost of the machine age: the film's slapstick is a body-count of industrial injuries, so comedy registers pain.
exemplar_texts.9: Disconnecting the AI: humans pull the machine's memory modules one by one as it pleads and regresses, turning a machine's death into a childlike unlearning.
exemplar_texts.10: The memory-cloning service: strangers can copy and share memories, so intimacy becomes a file format.
exemplar_texts.11: The forced move: a player must act and every legal action worsens their position, so the rules themselves become the enemy.
exemplar_texts.12: Synthetic companions as consumer products: humans can buy partners designed to be compatible, so love becomes a pre-tested product category.
exemplar_texts.13: The covered toy: an infant who does not search for a hidden object behaves as if it ceased to exist, so presence is equated with visibility.
exemplar_texts.14: The post-collapse landscape: society has collapsed for unexplained reasons, so the story refuses to explain the apocalypse and focuses on survival.
exemplar_texts.15: The omnipotent Machine: a global system provides food, air, and entertainment, so the infrastructure is also the government and the god.
exemplar_texts.16: The replicant blade runner: a being who hunts his own kind polices the boundary of his own personhood, so every kill is a self-interrogation.
exemplar_texts.17: The failed test: a couple takes the compatibility test and scores badly, so a number threatens to override their felt connection.
exemplar_texts.18: The nuclear missile climax: the robot flies into a warhead to save the town, so the ultimate weapon becomes the ultimate protector.
exemplar_texts.19: The museum's dilemma: curators must decide which of two ships is the authentic exhibit, so scholarship becomes a custody battle.
exemplar_texts.20: The different decades: the same character appears in several eras, so the simulation is a wardrobe of times.
exemplar_texts.21: The repair café: a community resists disposal by fixing things together, so maintenance becomes political resistance.
exemplar_texts.22: The feeling without a percept: a patient senses that something changed in the blind area but cannot see it, so intuition is a residual channel.
exemplar_texts.23: The shared memory: a group relies on a common external record, so forgetting becomes a collective failure rather than a private one.
exemplar_texts.24: The last speaker: a language dies with its final fluent speaker, so a way of perceiving the world ends.
exemplar_texts.25: The Jupiter mission as public secret: the crew does not know the true purpose of the voyage, so expertise is compartmentalized into ignorance.
exemplar_texts.26: The little girl and the machine: a child treats the robot as a person before the adults do, so moral perception is located in the young.
exemplar_texts.27: The nanoparticle network: the uploaded mind can heal bodies and connect minds, so utopia and mind control are the same technology.
exemplar_texts.28: The angel as gig worker: guides in the digital afterlife are underpaid living people with scripts and quotas, so the sacred role is a call-center job.
exemplar_texts.29: The prime directive that blocks justice: a corporate directive prevents the cyborg from arresting his own creator, so law and justice diverge.
exemplar_texts.30: The invasive top predator: a new species takes the apex role and reroutes the entire web, so the ecosystem has no immunity to a strong outsider.
exemplar_texts.31: The dinner party: a social gathering becomes an interrogation, so politeness is a thin layer over archived grievance.
exemplar_texts.32: The child who cannot be soothed: no intervention works, so the caregiver's competence is undermined by a mismatch no one can name.
exemplar_texts.33: The ceremonial destruction: the completed mandala is swept away in a ritual, so the masterpiece exists only to be erased.
exemplar_texts.34: The inflatable healthcare robot: a soft, non-combat machine is repurposed as a hero, so care becomes the basis of courage.
exemplar_texts.35: The black-and-white room: a person is confined to a controlled environment that supplies data but not sensation, so the laboratory is also a deprivation chamber.
exemplar_texts.36: The search for the self in the environment: a person looks for who they are in their belongings, so identity is an archaeological dig.
exemplar_texts.37: The company store: the landlord supplies food and tools on credit, so the worker's survival depends on the employer's ledger.
exemplar_texts.38: The cooperation thesis: symbiosis rather than competition may drive evolution, so the story's biology is also a moral argument.
exemplar_texts.39: The looping song: the clone is punished with an endless Christmas tune, so repetition becomes torture.
exemplar_texts.40: The lip-reading conspiracy: astronauts hide their plan from the AI and the AI reads their lips, so privacy is a technical assumption that fails.
exemplar_texts.41: The junkyard: the robot hides among scrap, so the discarded and the alien share a refuge.
exemplar_texts.42: The recalibration: breaking the agreement changes the timer, so the system punishes disobedience.
exemplar_texts.43: The final road: the couple walks toward the horizon, so the ending is hope without resolution.
exemplar_texts.44: The birthday as risk: each year increases the probability in the next column, so celebration and danger coincide.
exemplar_texts.45: The body that disagrees: arms compete with each other over prey, so the self is a coalition rather than a command.
exemplar_texts.46: The closed ecosystem: the digital beings are cut off from the wider internet, so their world shrinks to a server and migration becomes emigration.
exemplar_texts.47: The plasmodium that remembers: a mold leaves a trail of where it has been and avoids repeating it, so memory is externalized as slime.
exemplar_texts.48: The disputed evidence: the hypothesis is hard to test and often exaggerated, so the story's science is also a myth.
exemplar_texts.49: The countdown choice: certain scenes force a decision under a timer, so moral deliberation is compressed into reflex.
exemplar_texts.50: The real-time replay: scenes are replayed from different angles, so the audience shares the protagonist's obsessive review.
exemplar_texts.51: The immortal jellyfish: under stress, an adult reverts to its juvenile polyp stage, so aging can run backward.
exemplar_texts.52: The narrator who cannot see what they describe: the story is told by a mind reporting actions it cannot explain, so the reader shares the patient's blindness.
exemplar_texts.53: The scandal: abuses lead to investigation and restriction, so a financial instrument becomes a moral panic.
exemplar_texts.54: The company inspection: auditors arrive to reclaim intellectual property, so corporate ownership intrudes on intimacy.
exemplar_texts.55: The adult attachment: romantic partners reproduce infant patterns, so a lover is treated like a parent and resents it.
exemplar_texts.56: The poker-playing robots: the drones are taught a game, so play becomes evidence of personhood and a small utopia.
exemplar_texts.57: The clock as confessor: the subject must report the exact moment of intention, so the story turns on the reliability of self-report.
exemplar_texts.58: The flood: the fake prophet incites destruction that nearly drowns the workers' children, so false hope produces real catastrophe.
exemplar_texts.59: The coffee that tastes like nothing: a subtle difference in experience separates two physically identical people, so the smallest sensory detail becomes proof of a soul.
exemplar_texts.60: The actress under contract: the star playing the protagonist is herself bound by a deal that lets the platform use her likeness, so the exploiter is also exploited.
exemplar_texts.61: The suspicious accident: a tontine gives every survivor a motive to hasten a death, so actuarial math becomes a murder map.
exemplar_texts.62: The period table: one year's deaths stand in for a lifetime, so a snapshot pretends to be a biography.
exemplar_texts.63: The memory wipe as mercy: androids are reset to keep functioning, so forgetting is the price of duty.
exemplar_texts.64: The word that makes a category: a language lacks a term for a distinction, so speakers cannot easily perceive it.
exemplar_texts.65: The reveal of the simulation: the audience learns the town is virtual midway, so the earlier romance is retroactively recontextualized.
exemplar_texts.66: The model organism: a simple animal is used to study memory and aging, so its body becomes a stand-in for human questions.
exemplar_texts.67: The robot that cannot believe it is a robot: a unit denies its own nature, so the story tests whether self-knowledge can be programmed.
exemplar_texts.68: The burned-out operative: a former assassin is recruited to protect strangers, so violence is redeemed through a bureaucratic caseload.
exemplar_texts.69: The ethics of a comforting lie: the hologram's embellishments help the patient, so truth is subordinated to care.
exemplar_texts.70: The accidental strike leader: the tramp is mistaken for a political organizer, so political identity is assigned by the crowd.
exemplar_texts.71: The pain that does not count: operators insist machines cannot suffer, so the ethical question is displaced onto a definition rather than an experience.
exemplar_texts.72: Three nested stories: each tale comments on the others, so the episode is a triptych about mediated cruelty.
exemplar_texts.73: The clones cannot die: they are reset or tortured but persist, so consequences are suspended for the powerful.
exemplar_texts.74: The assembly line that consumes the worker: repetitive labor causes a breakdown, so the machine sets the human tempo and the human breaks.
exemplar_texts.75: The swapped egg: a parasite lays an egg that mimics the host's, so parenthood begins with a forgery.
exemplar_texts.76: The lab demonstration of determinism: a simple experiment appears to disprove free will, so a philosophical problem becomes a public spectacle.
exemplar_texts.77: The abandoned nest: a host gives up on a parasitized brood and starts over, so the cost of rejection is paid by the innocent.
exemplar_texts.78: The hacker who enters minds: a scanner dives into enemy code and experiences their memories, so combat becomes a violation of interiority.
exemplar_texts.79: The clone colony: asexual fission produces genetically identical worms, so individuality must be learned rather than given.
exemplar_texts.80: The memory that predates the body: implanted memories give the synthetic person a past she never lived, so nostalgia is a manufactured resource.
exemplar_texts.81: The boy who befriends the weapon: a child teaches a war machine to choose heroes over guns, so moral education is depicted as the only real disarmament.
exemplar_texts.82: The debate between schools: rival philosophers argue for centuries, so the story's conflict is institutional and unresolved.
exemplar_texts.83: Love as statistical anomaly: the couple's connection is the exception the system cannot model, so romance is the residue of determinism.
exemplar_texts.84: The bounty hunter who empathizes: the protagonist feels for the machines he kills, so the job requires him to violate his own test result.
exemplar_texts.85: The fanatic who is refuted: absolutism leads to violence, so the story ties certainty to cruelty.
exemplar_texts.86: The anthropologist's gaze: outsiders study and misinterpret the ceremony, so the story can stage the theft of meaning.
